План есть - можно работать

# App Store + Hugging Face + Remote Access («Your Reachies») + виджеты — Phase 2 finale

## Context

Последний крупный блок Фазы 2. По результатам ресёрча (исходники демона 1.9.0/main, открытый
central-сервер, официальные приложения Pollen) фича состоит из четырёх частей:

1. **Магазин приложений робота** — HF Spaces с тегом `reachy_mini_python_app`; демон сам
   скачивает snapshot и ставит `uv pip install` в общий venv. Клиент — обёртка над `/api/apps/*`.
2. **Вход в Hugging Face** — нативный, на телефоне, «в 1 кнопку» (как в официальном
   iOS-приложении, которое показывает вход до подключения к роботу ⇒ OAuth у него клиентский):
   `ASWebAuthenticationSession` (делит куки Safari) + наш зарегистрированный **public OAuth-app
   HF** (client_id без секрета, custom-scheme redirect, PKCE). Токен — в **Keychain**
   (ADR-0001: «credentials в Keychain, инжектятся централизованно ReachyKit»). Привязка робота =
   `POST /api/hf-auth/save-token` по LAN (демон валидирует через whoami и хранит у себя).
   Браузерный OAuth-флоу демона (редирект на `reachy-mini.local`) **не используем** — не нужен.
   Fallback без OAuth-app: вставка PAT.
3. **Remote-доступ «Your Reachies»** — central-сервер = публичный HF Space
   `https://pollen-robotics-reachy-mini-central.hf.space` (исходники открыты; env
   `REACHY_CENTRAL_URL`). Робот и клиент аутентифицируются `Authorization: Bearer <HF-токен>`;
   робот-producer виден только владельцу токена. Сигналинг — тот же протокол GStreamer
   webrtcsink, что у нас на :8443 (`SignalingMessage`), но поверх **SSE (`GET /events`) +
   `POST /send`**. Дальше обычный WebRTC (STUN-only, **TURN нет**). Удалённо HTTP-API демона
   **недоступен**: управление — data-канал `"data"` (JSON-команды `wake_up`, `set_target`,
   `get_state`… + JSON-RPC `apps.*`), телеметрия — unreliable-канал `"pose"` (~30 Hz, `seq`).
4. **Виджеты** — App Group + App Intents + widget-extension «запустить приложение робота».

Решения пользователя: всё в одной ветке `claude/hugging-face-oauth-app-store-5hu2g2`
(от `main@9404f7d`); вход — 1 кнопка + PAT-fallback; каталог — только демон (без кэш-API сайта).
Conventional commits, коммит на milestone.

## Контракт демона `/api/apps/*` (1.9.0; факты, проверенные по исходникам)

- `AppInfo{name, source_kind: hf_space|dashboard_selection|local|installed, description, url?, extra}` —
  `extra` = сырой JSON HF Space. **POST /install требует весь `AppInfo` дословно** → домен
  хранит оригинальный generated-объект для round-trip.
- **Ловушка идентичности**: catalog `name` = слаг Space, `extra["id"]` = `"owner/repo"`;
  installed `name` = имя pip entry-point (может отличаться!) — lifecycle-роуты ключуются по
  **installed**-имени. Сопоставлять через `extra["id"]` + нормализацию.
- `install|remove|update` → сразу `{"job_id"}`; **провал job — не HTTP-ошибка** (только
  `JobInfo.status == failed`). `job_id` не переживает рестарт демона (404).
- WS `/api/apps/ws/apps-manager/{job_id}` (не в spec): неизвестный id →
  `{"error":"Job ID not found"}`+close; каждая новая строка лога — голый текстовый фрейм, затем
  JSON `{command,status,logs:[новые]}`; закрывается после done|failed; **просыпается только на
  новых логах** → может молча висеть — всегда в паре с поллингом `job-status` (500 ms; таймауты:
  install 60 s, remove 90 s, stale 90 s).
- `current-app-status` → **200 с литеральным `null`**, когда idle. `stop-current-app` повторно →
  400. `start-app` при занятом слоте → 400. `no-evict` — только main (404 на 1.9.0), не используем.
  `GET /api/daemon/robot-app-lock-status` → `{state: free|local_app|remote_session, holder_name?}`.
- `check-updates?force=` — кэш 5 мин на демоне.
- UI-метаданные из `extra`: `cardData{title, emoji, colorFrom, colorTo, short_description}`,
  `author`, `likes`, `private`; official = `author == "pollen-robotics"`. Тумбнейлов нет —
  эмодзи на градиенте.
- hf-auth: `GET /hf-auth/status → {is_logged_in, username?}` (whoami на каждый вызов — медленно
  → кэшировать); `POST /hf-auth/save-token {token}` (400 если невалиден); `DELETE /hf-auth/token`;
  `GET /hf-auth/central-robot-status → {available, robots[], reason?}` (LAN-прокси central без
  выдачи токена); `GET /hf-auth/relay-status → {state: stopped|waiting_for_token|connecting|connected|reconnecting|error, is_connected}`;
  `POST /hf-auth/refresh-relay`. Все ответы кроме save-token в спеке `additionalProperties: true`
  → generated отдаёт `OpenAPIObjectContainer`, декодировать руками (паттерн `kinematicsInfo()`).

## Контракт central-сервера (из `app.py` Space `pollen-robotics/reachy_mini_central`)

- Auth: только `Authorization: Bearer` (валидация через `whoami-v2`, кэшируется). Rate limit
  1200 req/60 s на токен. `GET /health` — без auth.
- `GET /api/robot-status` → `{robots: [{peerId, robotName?, busy, activeApp?, meta{name, transport,
  hardware_id?, install_id?}, last_seen_age_seconds}]}`. **Онлайн = присутствие в списке**
  (lease 30 s, heartbeat робота ~10 s). `peerId` меняется на каждом реконнекте relay —
  стабильный ключ: `install_id ?? hardware_id ?? peerId`; `hardware_id` = тот же 16-hex, что
  `GET /api/daemon/hardware-id` (правило 4 — join LAN↔central по нему).
- Сигналинг: `GET /events` (SSE, `data:`-строки; `welcome{peerId, username,
  recommended_heartbeat_interval_seconds}` → `list{producers[]}` → дельты `peerStatusChanged`,
  `sessionStateChanged`; `ping` каждые 30 s — тишина >30 s = мёртвый стрим). Исходящее —
  `POST /send`, **ответ приходит телом POST** (`sessionStarted{sessionId}` /
  `sessionRejected{reason: robot_busy, activeApp}` / `error{details}`). Клиент представляется
  `setPeerStatus{roles:["listener"], meta:{name}}` — `meta.name` виден владельцу как `activeApp`.
- **Робот — offerer**: по SSE приходит `peer{sessionId, sdp:{offer}}` → отвечаем
  `peer{sdp:{answer}}`; ICE `peer{ice:{…}}` в обе стороны; **пустой `candidate` =
  end-of-candidates — дропать** (WebRTC.framework кидает на нём). `endSession{reason:
  robot_busy|robot_busy_local|robot_busy_local_app|local_app_started|install_id_takeover}` —
  обрабатывать обе формы отказа (`sessionRejected` и `endSession`).
- ICE: STUN-only `stun:stun.l.google.com:19302`, **TURN нет** — симметричный NAT/CGNAT не
  соберётся; таймаут → подсказка «подключитесь к одной сети».
- Медиа: H.264 CB 3.1 видео + **двунаправленный** Opus (робот форсирует `sendrecv`).
- Data-каналы: `"data"` (reliable, открывает робот) — JSON-команды
  (`{"type": "wake_up"}`, `get_state → {state:{head[16], antennas, body_yaw, motor_mode,
  is_move_running}}`, `set_target`, volume, robot-name, …) и JSON-RPC 2.0
  (`apps.start|stop|install|status`; прочие namespace уходят в запущенное приложение);
  `"pose"` (unreliable, приходит вторым `ondatachannel` после `subscribe_pose`) — ~30 Hz,
  дропать `seq <= lastSeq`, команды туда не слать.
- `local_app` на роботе ≠ «нельзя подключиться»: сессия принимается как control-only.

---

# Milestones

## M1 — ReachyKit: домен + клиент приложений

- `Sources/ReachyKit/Model/RobotApps.swift` — `RobotApp` (обёртка над generated
  `Components.Schemas.AppInfo` + парсинг `extra`: `spaceID`, `title`, `emoji`, `gradient`,
  `author`, `likes`, `isPrivate`, `isOfficial`), `RobotAppStatus` (state с `unknown(String)` —
  не кидает), `StartupApp`, `AppUpdatesSummary`, `RobotAppLockStatus`, маппинг идентичности
  `RobotApp.matches(installed:)`.
- `Sources/ReachyKit/Model/DaemonUpdate.swift` — извлечь общий `DaemonJob`
  (`typealias DaemonUpdateJob = DaemonJob`): app-jobs и update-jobs делят shape и `isTerminal`.
- `Sources/ReachyKit/Session/RobotAppsClient.swift` — протокол с throwing-defaults (образец
  `DaemonUpdateClient`); конформанс в `Transport/RobotConnection+Apps.swift` через
  generated-клиент (`currentAppStatus`: null-body → `nil`).
- `Sources/ReachyKit/Transport/AppsManagerStreamClient.swift` — WS по образцу
  `UpdateLogStreamClient` (события `line|status|rejected|closed`, ровно один `.closed`;
  try-JSON-decode каждого фрейма, не-JSON = строка лога).
- `Sources/ReachyKit/Session/AppJobMonitor.swift` — WS + поллинг `job-status` 500 ms
  (инжектируемый clock — правило 7), таймауты 60/90/90 s, исход «демон перезапустился» (404
  после видимого старта).
- `Sources/ReachyKit/Session/RobotSession+Apps.swift` — `canManageApps`, `withAppsClient {}`
  (копия `withWiFiClient`), кэш каталога/installed (образец `moves(in:refresh:)`).

Тесты: `StubURLProtocol` (null-body, 400 на повторный stop, дословный round-trip `AppInfo` в
теле install — по записанному запросу), `LocalWebSocketServer` (фреймы-причуды, тихое
завершение → добор поллингом), идентичность, `.timeLimit(.minutes(1))` на async-тестах.

## M2 — ReachyKit: hf-auth-поверхность демона

- `Sources/ReachyKit/Model/HFAuth.swift` — `HFAuthStatus{isLoggedIn, username?}`,
  `RelayStatus{state, isConnected, message?}` (state с `unknown(String)`),
  `CentralRobotStatusProxy{available, robots, reason?}`.
- `Sources/ReachyKit/Session/HFAuthClient.swift` + `Transport/RobotConnection+HFAuth.swift` —
  `hfAuthStatus()`, `saveHFToken(_:)`, `deleteHFToken()`, `centralRobotStatus()`,
  `relayStatus()`, `refreshRelay()`; ручное декодирование `OpenAPIObjectContainer`
  (re-encode → `JSONDecoder`, как `kinematicsInfo`). OAuth-роуты демона не оборачиваем.
- `Sources/ReachyKit/Session/RobotSession+HFAuth.swift` — `robotHFAccount` (кэшированный
  статус), `linkRobot(token:)` (save-token + refresh-relay), `unlinkRobot()`.

Тесты: фикстуры всех состояний, токен только в JSON-body (запись `StubURLProtocol`),
неизвестные значения → `unknown`.

## M3 — ReachyKit: нативный вход в HF (клиентский токен)

- **Пререквизит (руками, вне кода)**: зарегистрировать public OAuth-app на
  `huggingface.co/settings/applications/new` — без секрета, redirect
  `reachy-mini-swift://oauth-callback`, scopes `openid profile read-repos write-repos
  manage-repos inference-api` (совпадают с тем, что просит робот — один токен на всё).
  client_id — константа в коде; пока его нет, работает PAT-путь.
- `Sources/ReachyKit/Auth/HFTokenStore.swift` — Keychain (`kSecClassGenericPassword`,
  Security framework, без сторонних зависимостей): токен, username, expiry, refresh_token?.
  Первый Keychain-код в проекте — предписан ADR-0001.
- `Sources/ReachyKit/Auth/HFOAuth.swift` — чистая логика без UI: PKCE (CryptoKit SHA256),
  сборка authorize-URL (`URLComponents` — правило 5), обмен кода
  (`POST https://huggingface.co/oauth/token`), декодинг (`access_token`/`accessToken` — демон
  страхуется от обоих ключей, повторить), refresh при наличии refresh_token, иначе — флаг
  `needsReauth` по expiry.
- `Sources/ReachyKit/Auth/HFAccount.swift` — `@MainActor @Observable` модель аккаунта:
  signed-out / signing-in / signed-in(username, avatarURL) / needsReauth; инжектируемые seams
  (store, exchanger, browser) для тестов и превью.
- Валидация PAT: `GET https://huggingface.co/api/whoami-v2` (то же, чем пользуется central).

Тесты: PKCE-вектора, обмен/refresh через `StubURLProtocol`, Keychain-store за протоколом
(In-memory double), модель состояний.

## M4 — ReachyUI: экран магазина

- `Sources/ReachyUI/Apps/AppStoreModel.swift` + `AppStoreScreen.swift` — секции
  Installed / Discover (сегментный Picker, coalescing `loadID: UUID` — образец `MovesModel`),
  поиск, карточка (эмодзи на градиенте, title, author, likes, Official, замочек private),
  running-баннер (Stop/Restart), тумблер startup-app, бейджи обновлений, учёт
  `robot-app-lock-status` (`remote_session` → объяснение).
- `AppInstallModel.swift` + `AppInstallOverlay.swift` — образец `SystemUpdateModel`: State-enum
  (idle/installing/removing/updating/confirming/succeeded/failed/daemonRestarted), живой лог
  через `LogConsoleModel`, движок `AppJobMonitor`; после `done` — подтверждающий поллинг
  installed-списка; сеams для тестов/превью.
- Запуск при занятом слоте: `confirmationDialog` «остановить X и запустить Y?» (stop → start).
- Приватные Spaces: если `isPrivate` и робот не привязан — подсказка со ссылкой на вход (M6).
- Навигация: `NavigationLink("Apps")` в `RobotScreen.controlSection` за `canManageApps`.

Превью (правило 8): store — loading/empty/catalog/installed+running/offline; overlay —
installing/failed/success. `test:snapshots:record` + явный `git add` PNG (LFS).
Тесты моделей в `Tests/ReachyUITests`.

## M5 — Виджеты: фундамент + extension

- App Group `group.com.alexey1312.ReachyMini` в `Apps/Project.swift` (ReachySpike + новый таргет).
- `Sources/ReachyKit/Model/SharedRobotSnapshot.swift` — `{address, hardwareID, robotName,
  installedApps[{name, title, emoji}], currentAppName, updatedAt}` через
  `UserDefaults(suiteName:)`; `RobotSession` пишет на connect/после операций.
- `Sources/ReachyKit/Widget/WidgetRobotClient.swift` — минимальный клиент интентов
  (currentAppStatus/startApp/stopCurrentApp, timeout ~4 s, `URLComponents`).
- `Apps/ReachySpike/Sources/Intents/` — `RobotAppEntity` (+ query из снапшота),
  `StartRobotAppIntent`, `StopRobotAppIntent`; ошибка сети → понятный текст «откройте
  приложение».
- Таргет `ReachyWidgets` (`Apps/ReachyWidgets/`, iOS-only, bundleId
  `com.alexey1312.ReachyMiniSpike.widgets`): конфигурируемый виджет «запустить приложение»
  (`Button(intent:)`) + текущее running-app из снапшота; ReachySpike embed'ит его.
- Риск: Local Network в extension-процессе iOS ненадёжен — деградация в понятную ошибку.
  Widget UI вне снапшот-матрицы — отметить как осознанно непокрытое (правило 8).

## M6 — ReachyUI: вход и аккаунт HF

- `Sources/ReachyUI/Settings/HFAccountSection.swift` — карточка в Settings (образец
  `WiFiSettingsCard`): signed-out → «Sign in with Hugging Face» (+ вторичная «Paste token»);
  signed-in → username + аватар (`https://huggingface.co/api/users/{username}/avatar`),
  состояние привязки текущего робота (`robotHFAccount`) + кнопка «Link this robot»
  (save-token по LAN — предупреждение про plain HTTP), relay-статус робота, Sign out
  (локально; отвязка робота — отдельно, `unlinkRobot`).
- `Sources/ReachyUI/Settings/HFSignInModel.swift` + `HFSignInFlow.swift` — «1 кнопка»:
  `ASWebAuthenticationSession` (не-ephemeral → куки Safari → мгновенно для залогиненных) через
  `@MainActor` protocol-seam в ReachyUI (модель тестируема без браузера, превью не открывают
  окон — `reachyPreviewMode`); callback по custom-scheme → обмен кода в M3; исходы
  success/cancelled/error; PAT-шаг (SecureField) — fallback и путь без client_id. Каркас —
  `OnboardingStepScaffold`.
- Первый вход предлагать контекстно: из магазина (private Space) и из «Your Reachies» (M9).

Превью: карточка signed-out/signed-in/linked/needsReauth; флоу — start/browser/PAT/success/error.
Тесты: HFSignInModelTests на фейковом browser-seam.

## M7 — ReachyKit: клиент central-сервера

- `Sources/ReachyKit/Central/CentralRelayClient.swift` — `URLSession.bytes` + `.lines` на
  `GET /events` (парсить только `data:`-строки, не требовать `event:`), исходящее
  `POST /send` с декодом **тела ответа** как сигнального сообщения; keepalive-надзор
  (тишина >30 s = реконнект с backoff — образец `StateStreamClient`); Bearer из
  `HFTokenStore` инжектится централизованно (ADR-0001).
- Расширить `SignalingMessage` (`Sources/ReachyKit/Transport/`): `welcome`, `list` (+`busy`,
  `activeApp`), `peerStatusChanged`, `sessionStateChanged`, `sessionStarted`,
  `sessionRejected{reason, activeApp?}`, `endSession{reason?}`, `error{details}` — decode
  снисходительный (правило 3).
- `Sources/ReachyKit/Central/CentralRobot.swift` — модель строки списка; стабильный ключ
  `install_id ?? hardware_id ?? peerId`; сортировка по `last_seen_age_seconds`.
- `Sources/ReachyKit/Central/YourReachiesModel`-уровень: `listRobots()` (REST) + live-обновления
  из SSE-дельт.

Тесты: SSE-поток через `StubURLProtocol` со стрим-ответом (при необходимости — маленький
`LocalHTTPServer` harness рядом с `LocalWebSocketServer`), обе формы отказа, пустой ICE-candidate,
rate-limit 429 → backoff.

## M8 — ReachyKit/ReachyMedia: удалённая сессия (транспорт)

- Seam сигналинга: протокол `SignalingTransport` — существующий WS :8443
  (`CameraSignalingClient`) и новый `CentralSignalingTransport` (M7) — RTC-половина не меняется
  (робот offerer, мы answerer, STUN-only), переиспользуется стек `ReachyMedia`.
- `Sources/ReachyKit/Central/RemoteControlChannel.swift` — канал `"data"`: JSON-команды
  (запрос/ответ `{"status":"ok"}` или payload-конверт) + JSON-RPC 2.0 (`apps.*`, id-корреляция,
  ошибки `reason`); канал `"pose"` — отдельный AsyncStream с dedup по `seq`.
- `RemoteRobotConnection` — конформит **те же capability-протоколы**, что `RobotConnection`,
  где поверхность есть удалённо: `RobotAPIClient` (wake/sleep/state/volume/robot-name через
  команды), `RobotAppsClient` (через `apps.*` JSON-RPC). **Не** конформит `WiFiConfigClient`,
  `DaemonUpdateClient` → существующие capability-флаги сами прячут недоступное (в этом смысл
  расслоения протоколов). `RobotSession.makeClient` уже инжектируем — remote = другая фабрика.
- Состояние стриминга: удалённо `state` приходит по `"pose"`-каналу → адаптер под интерфейс
  `StateStreamClient` для `ViewportModel`.
- Опасные команды (`restart_daemon`, `start_update`, `delete_hf_token`) удалённо в UI **не
  выносить**, пока не проверено гейтирование (зафиксировано как открытый вопрос).

Тесты: RPC-корреляция и ошибки, pose-dedup, маппинг протоколов на дублях; e2e — только ручное.

## M9 — ReachyUI: «Your Reachies» + remote-подключение

- `Sources/ReachyUI/Central/YourReachiesScreen.swift` + модель: signed-out (CTA на вход M6),
  список роботов (имя, online по присутствию, busy/activeApp, Wireless/USB-бейдж), Refresh,
  пусто («привяжите робота» → подсказка), джойн LAN↔central по `hardware_id` — один робот не
  показывается дважды (правило 4).
- Подключение: степпер **LINK → SESSION → WAKE-UP** (дизайн-ориентир — официальное приложение;
  реализация — расширение `ConnectionStepper`), статусные подписи («Establishing the WebRTC
  session»…), исходы: `robot_busy(activeApp)`, NAT-таймаут («подключитесь к одной сети»),
  эвикция по `endSession{reason}` — понятные тексты.
- Интеграция в `ConnectionScreen`/`RobotBrowser`: central — второй источник роботов рядом с
  LAN-discovery; remote-бейдж в шапке `RobotScreen`; latency/путь (LAN vs Remote) в
  инфо-карточке.
- Превью: список (signed-out/empty/online/busy), степпер по шагам, отказы.

## M10 — Документация

- `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-04-app-store-hf-remote-design.md` — формат существующих
  спеков (Shape-таблица по milestone'ам).
- `docs/adr/0003-hf-token-custody.md` — два хранителя токена: Keychain на клиенте (нативный
  OAuth public-app + PKCE; PAT-fallback) и робот (`save-token`); central доверяет любому
  валидному токену; plain-HTTP LAN при привязке — принятое ограничение (ADR-0001);
  browser-flow и device-flow демона отвергнуты (не нужны при нативном входе).
- `docs/research/central-relay.md` — протокол central-сервера (SSE+POST, сообщения, data-каналы,
  открытые вопросы: `install_id`, гейтирование опасных команд, ротация токена = новый peer).
- Дополнить `.claude/rules/daemon-api.md` (apps-WS причуды, идентичность, null-body,
  версионный скью) и `.claude/rules/networking.md` (central, STUN-only, обе формы отказа).
- README: Status Фазы 2.

## Порядок и зависимости

M1 → M2 → M3 (независим от M1–M2) → M4 (нужен M1) → M5 (нужен M1) → M6 (нужны M2+M3) →
M7 (нужен M3) → M8 (нужны M7 + ReachyMedia) → M9 (нужны M6–M8) → M10. Каждый milestone
собирается/тестируется и коммитится отдельно; ветка публикуется целиком.

## Верификация

1. `./bin/mise run build` / `test` после каждого milestone (после правок тестов —
   `swift build --build-tests`, не `--skip-build`).
2. `./bin/mise run test:snapshots` → `record` для новых превью, явный `git add` PNG;
   генерирующую задачу — последней (16-pin `Package.resolved`).
3. `./bin/mise run build:app` — ReachySpike + ReachyWidgets.
4. `sim-daemon` + `test:sim` (за `REACHY_SIM_HOST`): `list-available` декодируется,
   `current-app-status` = nil, `job-status/unknown` = 404, `hf-auth/status` = logged-out.
   Реальную установку в интеграционных тестах не делать. `central-robot-status` на sim без
   токена → `reason: not_authenticated` — тоже проверить.
5. `GET https://pollen-robotics-reachy-mini-central.hf.space/health` — живой смоук central
   (без токена); контрактные тесты central — только на фикстурах (не бить боевой сервер из CI).
6. `./bin/mise run lint`, `format-check`.
7. Ручное на железе (PR-чеклист): install/запуск/стоп, вход в 1 кнопку (Safari залогинен/нет),
   привязка робота + появление в «Your Reachies», remote-сессия с мобильного интернета
   (и NAT-фейл → подсказка), эвикция локальным приложением, Local Network из widget-extension.

## Риски

- **NAT без TURN** — remote может не собраться (CGNAT/симметричный NAT); честный таймаут и
  подсказка. Продуктовое ограничение всего стека Pollen, не наше.
- Версионный скью демона: `no-evict`/device-flow только в main — не используем; `install_id`
  в meta может не приходить с 1.9.0 — ключ каскадный.
- WS job-стрима может молча висеть → `AppJobMonitor` всегда поллит параллельно; рестарт демона
  теряет job → отдельный исход + подтверждение по installed-списку.
- OAuth: client_id надо зарегистрировать руками (до этого — PAT); expiry без refresh_token →
  `needsReauth` (повторный вход почти мгновенен через куки Safari). Ротация токена = новый peer
  на central (кэш по строке токена).
- Rate limit central 1200/60 s → никакого агрессивного поллинга, SSE-дельты вместо refresh.
- Опасные remote-команды не выносим в UI до проверки гейтирования.
- PAT/токен по plain HTTP LAN при привязке — предупреждение в UI, тест «не в query».
- Local Network в widget-extension — подтверждается только устройством.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/aleksei/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/superpowers/6.2.0/skills/executing-plans

# Executing Plans

## Overview

Load plan, review critically, execute all tasks, report when complete.

**Announce at start:** "I'm using the executing-plans skill to implement this plan."

**Note:** Tell your human partner that Superpowers works much better with access to subagents (Claude Code, Codex CLI, Codex App, Copilot CLI, and Gemini CLI all qualify; see the per-platform tool refs in `../using-superpowers/references/`). If subagents are available, use superpowers:subagent-driven-development instead of this skill.

## The Process

### Step 1: Load and Review Plan
1. Ensure an isolated workspace: use superpowers:using-git-worktrees to create one or verify the existing one
2. Read plan file
3. Review critically - identify any questions or concerns about the plan
4. If concerns: Raise them with your human partner before starting
5. If no concerns: Create todos for the plan items and proceed

### Step 2: Execute Tasks

For each task:
1. Mark as in_progress
2. Follow each step exactly (plan has bite-sized steps)
3. Run verifications as specified
4. Mark as completed

### Step 3: Complete Development

After all tasks complete and verified:
- Announce: "I'm using the finishing-a-development-branch skill to complete this work."
- **REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** Use superpowers:finishing-a-development-branch
- Follow that skill to verify tests, present options, execute choice

## When to Stop and Ask for Help

**STOP executing immediately when:**
- Hit a blocker (missing dependency, test fails, instruction unclear)
- Plan has critical gaps preventing starting
- You don't understand an instruction
- Verification fails repeatedly

**Ask for clarification rather than guessing.**

## When to Revisit Earlier Steps

**Return to Review (Step 1) when:**
- Partner updates the plan based on your feedback
- Fundamental approach needs rethinking

**Don't force through blockers** - stop and ask.

## Remember
- Review plan critically first
- Follow plan steps exactly
- Don't skip verifications
- Reference skills when plan says to
- Stop when blocked, don't guess
- Never start implementation on main/master branch without explicit user consent

2	import Network

4	/// Minimal in-process WebSocket server for transport tests.
5	/// Accepts connections on an ephemeral port, hands each one to `onConnection`.
6	final class LocalWebSocketServer: @unchecked Sendable {
7	    private let listener: NWListener
8	    private let queue = DispatchQueue(label: "LocalWebSocketServer")
9	
10	    var port: UInt16 {
11	        listener.port?.rawValue ?? 0
12	    }
13	
14	    init(onConnection: @escaping @Sendable (NWConnection) -> Void) throws {
15	        let parameters = NWParameters.tcp
16	        let wsOptions = NWProtocolWebSocket.Options()
17	        parameters.defaultProtocolStack.applicationProtocols.insert(wsOptions, at: 0)
18	        listener = try NWListener(using: parameters, on: .any)
19	        listener.newConnectionHandler = { connection in
20	            connection.start(queue: DispatchQueue(label: "LocalWebSocketServer.connection"))
21	            onConnection(connection)
22	        }
23	        listener.start(queue: queue)
24	    }
25	
26	    /// Waits until the listener is ready and returns its port.
27	    func readyPort() async throws -> UInt16 {
28	        while listener.state != .ready {
29	            try await Task.sleep(for: .milliseconds(10))
30	        }
31	        return port
32	    }
33	
34	    /// `then` runs once the frame is actually on the wire. A test that tears the
35	    /// connection down straight after the call would otherwise race the send and
36	    /// drop the very frame it is asserting on.
37	    static func sendText(_ text: String, over connection: NWConnection, then onSent: (@Sendable () -> Void)? = nil) {
38	        let metadata = NWProtocolWebSocket.Metadata(opcode: .text)
39	        let context = NWConnection.ContentContext(identifier: "text", metadata: [metadata])
40	        connection.send(
41	            content: Data(text.utf8),
42	            contentContext: context,
43	            isComplete: true,
44	            completion: onSent.map { sent in .contentProcessed { _ in sent() } } ?? .idempotent
45	        )
46	    }
47	
48	    func stop() {
49	        listener.cancel()
50	    }
51	}

2	"""Normalize the daemon OpenAPI spec for swift-openapi-generator.
3	
4	FastAPI/Pydantic v2 encodes nullable fields as `anyOf: [X, {"type": "null"}]`.
5	swift-openapi-generator does not support `type: null` branches (upstream issues
6	apple/swift-openapi-generator#906, #817) and silently drops such properties,
7	producing empty structs.
8	
9	Stripping the null branch alone is not enough: Pydantic marks `Optional[X]`
10	without a default as *required and nullable* (e.g. `DaemonStatus.backend_status`,
11	which a stopped daemon sends as null). Such a property must also leave `required`,
12	or the generated Swift field is non-Optional and decoding a real null throws.
13	
14	Usage: normalize-openapi.py <spec.json>   (rewrites the file in place)
15	"""
16	import json
17	import sys
18	
19	
20	def is_nullable(schema):
21	    return isinstance(schema, dict) and any(
22	        branch == {"type": "null"} for branch in schema.get("anyOf", [])
23	    )
24	
25	
26	def relax_nullable_required(node):
27	    """Drop required+nullable properties from `required`, before the null branch is gone."""
28	    if isinstance(node, list):
29	        for item in node:
30	            relax_nullable_required(item)
31	        return
32	    if not isinstance(node, dict):
33	        return
34	
35	    properties = node.get("properties")
36	    required = node.get("required")
37	    if isinstance(properties, dict) and isinstance(required, list):
38	        remaining = [name for name in required if not is_nullable(properties.get(name))]
39	        if remaining:
40	            node["required"] = remaining
41	        else:
42	            node.pop("required")
43	
44	    for value in node.values():
45	        relax_nullable_required(value)
46	
47	
48	def strip_null_branches(node):
49	    if isinstance(node, list):
50	        for item in node:
51	            strip_null_branches(item)
52	        return
53	    if not isinstance(node, dict):
54	        return
55	
56	    any_of = node.get("anyOf")
57	    if isinstance(any_of, list):
58	        remaining = [b for b in any_of if b != {"type": "null"}]
59	        if len(remaining) == 1:
60	            branch = remaining[0]
61	            node.pop("anyOf")
62	            if "$ref" in branch:
63	                # Bare $ref; siblings like `title` are dropped (ignored by 3.1 tools anyway)
64	                node.clear()
65	            node.update(branch)
66	        elif remaining:
67	            node["anyOf"] = remaining
68	
69	    for value in node.values():
70	        strip_null_branches(value)
71	
72	
73	def main():
74	    path = sys.argv[1]
75	    with open(path) as f:
76	        spec = json.load(f)
77	    relax_nullable_required(spec)
78	    strip_null_branches(spec)
79	    with open(path, "w") as f:
80	        json.dump(spec, f, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False)

# Test-Driven Development (TDD)

## Overview

Write the test first. Watch it fail. Write minimal code to pass.

**Core principle:** If you didn't watch the test fail, you don't know if it tests the right thing.

**Violating the letter of the rules is violating the spirit of the rules.**

## When to Use

**Always:**
- New features
- Bug fixes
- Refactoring
- Behavior changes

**Exceptions (ask your human partner):**
- Throwaway prototypes
- Generated code
- Configuration files

Thinking "skip TDD just this once"? Stop. That's rationalization.

## The Iron Law

```
NO PRODUCTION CODE WITHOUT A FAILING TEST FIRST
```

Write code before the test? Delete it. Start over.

**No exceptions:**
- Don't keep it as "reference"
- Don't "adapt" it while writing tests
- Don't look at it
- Delete means delete

Implement fresh from tests. Period.

## Red-Green-Refactor

```dot
digraph tdd_cycle {
    rankdir=LR;
    red [label="RED\nWrite failing test", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ffcccc"];
    verify_red [label="Verify fails\ncorrectly", shape=diamond];
    green [label="GREEN\nMinimal code", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ccffcc"];
    verify_green [label="Verify passes\nAll green", shape=diamond];
    refactor [label="REFACTOR\nClean up", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ccccff"];
    next [label="Next", shape=ellipse];

    red -> verify_red;
    verify_red -> green [label="yes"];
    verify_red -> red [label="wrong\nfailure"];
    green -> verify_green;
    verify_green -> refactor [label="yes"];
    verify_green -> green [label="no"];
    refactor -> verify_green [label="stay\ngreen"];
    verify_green -> next;
    next -> red;
}
```

### RED - Write Failing Test

Write one minimal test showing what should happen.

<Good>
```typescript
test('retries failed operations 3 times', async () => {
  let attempts = 0;
  const operation = () => {
    attempts++;
    if (attempts < 3) throw new Error('fail');
    return 'success';
  };

  const result = await retryOperation(operation);

  expect(result).toBe('success');
  expect(attempts).toBe(3);
});
```
Clear name, tests real behavior, one thing
</Good>

<Bad>
```typescript
test('retry works', async () => {
  const mock = jest.fn()
    .mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error())
    .mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error())
    .mockResolvedValueOnce('success');
  await retryOperation(mock);
  expect(mock).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(3);
});
```
Vague name, tests mock not code
</Bad>

**Requirements:**
- One behavior
- Clear name
- Real code (no mocks unless unavoidable)

### Verify RED - Watch It Fail

**MANDATORY. Never skip.**

```bash
npm test path/to/test.test.ts
```

Confirm:
- Test fails (not errors)
- Failure message is expected
- Fails because feature missing (not typos)

**Test passes?** You're testing existing behavior. Fix test.

**Test errors?** Fix error, re-run until it fails correctly.

### GREEN - Minimal Code

Write simplest code to pass the test.

<Good>
```typescript
async function retryOperation<T>(fn: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
  for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
    try {
      return await fn();
    } catch (e) {
      if (i === 2) throw e;
    }
  }
  throw new Error('unreachable');
}
```
Just enough to pass
</Good>

<Bad>
```typescript
async function retryOperation<T>(
  fn: () => Promise<T>,
  options?: {
    maxRetries?: number;
    backoff?: 'linear' | 'exponential';
    onRetry?: (attempt: number) => void;
  }
): Promise<T> {
  // YAGNI
}
```
Over-engineered
</Bad>

Don't add features, refactor other code, or "improve" beyond the test.

### Verify GREEN - Watch It Pass

**MANDATORY.**

```bash
npm test path/to/test.test.ts
```

Confirm:
- Test passes
- Other tests still pass
- Output pristine (no errors, warnings)

**Test fails?** Fix code, not test.

**Other tests fail?** Fix now.

### REFACTOR - Clean Up

After green only:
- Remove duplication
- Improve names
- Extract helpers

Keep tests green. Don't add behavior.

### Repeat

Next failing test for next feature.

## Good Tests

| Quality | Good | Bad |
|---------|------|-----|
| **Minimal** | One thing. "and" in name? Split it. | `test('validates email and domain and whitespace')` |
| **Clear** | Name describes behavior | `test('test1')` |
| **Shows intent** | Demonstrates desired API | Obscures what code should do |

When writing or changing any test, read [writing-good-tests.md](writing-good-tests.md) for the rules that keep tests honest:
- Name the production change that would make the test fail — before writing it
- Assert on real behavior, never on mock behavior
- Keep test-only code in test utilities, out of production classes
- Understand a dependency's side effects before mocking it

## Common Rationalizations

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "Too simple to test" | Simple code breaks. Test takes 30 seconds. |
| "I'll test after" | Tests written after pass immediately — which proves nothing. They may test the wrong thing, test the implementation instead of the behavior, or miss the edge case you forgot. You never watched it fail, so you never proved it can catch the bug. Test-first forces that failure. |
| "Tests after achieve same goals (spirit not ritual)" | Tests-after answer "what does this do?"; tests-first answer "what should this do?" Tests written after are biased by the code you already wrote — you verify the cases you remembered, not the ones you'd have discovered. Coverage without proof the tests work. |
| "Already manually tested" | Manual testing is ad-hoc: no record of what you covered, no way to re-run it when the code changes, easy to forget cases under pressure. "Worked when I tried it" ≠ comprehensive. Automated tests run the same way every time. |
| "Deleting X hours is wasteful" | Sunk cost fallacy — that time is already spent either way. The real choice: rewrite with TDD (high confidence) vs. keep it and bolt tests on after (low confidence, likely bugs). Keeping code you can't trust is the waste. |
| "Keep as reference, write tests first" | You'll adapt it. That's testing after. Delete means delete. |
| "Need to explore first" | Fine. Throw away exploration, start with TDD. |
| "Test hard = design unclear" | Listen to test. Hard to test = hard to use. |
| "TDD will slow me down" | TDD IS the pragmatic path: catches bugs before commit, prevents regressions, lets you refactor without fear. "Pragmatic" shortcuts mean debugging in production — slower, not faster. |
| "Manual test faster" | Manual doesn't prove edge cases. You'll re-test every change. |
| "Existing code has no tests" | You're improving it. Add tests for existing code. |

## Red Flags - STOP and Start Over

- Code before test
- Test after implementation
- Test passes immediately
- Can't explain why test failed
- Tests added "later"
- Rationalizing "just this once"
- "I already manually tested it"
- "Tests after achieve the same purpose"
- "It's about spirit not ritual"
- "Keep as reference" or "adapt existing code"
- "Already spent X hours, deleting is wasteful"
- "TDD is dogmatic, I'm being pragmatic"
- "This is different because..."

**All of these mean: Delete code. Start over with TDD.**

## Example: Bug Fix

**Bug:** Empty email accepted

**RED**
```typescript
test('rejects empty email', async () => {
  const result = await submitForm({ email: '' });
  expect(result.error).toBe('Email required');
});
```

**Verify RED**
```bash
$ npm test
FAIL: expected 'Email required', got undefined
```

**GREEN**
```typescript
function submitForm(data: FormData) {
  if (!data.email?.trim()) {
    return { error: 'Email required' };
  }
  // ...
}
```

**Verify GREEN**
```bash
$ npm test
PASS
```

**REFACTOR**
Extract validation for multiple fields if needed.

## Verification Checklist

Before marking work complete:

- [ ] Every new function/method has a test
- [ ] Watched each test fail before implementing
- [ ] Each test failed for expected reason (feature missing, not typo)
- [ ] Wrote minimal code to pass each test
- [ ] All tests pass
- [ ] Output pristine (no errors, warnings)
- [ ] Tests use real code (mocks only if unavoidable)
- [ ] Edge cases and errors covered

Can't check all boxes? You skipped TDD. Start over.

## When Stuck

| Problem | Solution |
|---------|----------|
| Don't know how to test | Write wished-for API. Write assertion first. Ask your human partner. |
| Test too complicated | Design too complicated. Simplify interface. |
| Must mock everything | Code too coupled. Use dependency injection. |
| Test setup huge | Extract helpers. Still complex? Simplify design. |

## Debugging Integration

Bug found? Write failing test reproducing it. Follow TDD cycle. Test proves fix and prevents regression.

Never fix bugs without a test.

## Final Rule

```
Production code → test exists and failed first
Otherwise → not TDD
```

No exceptions without your human partner's permission.

SpaceData = dict[str, object]


def _to_plain_json(value: object) -> object:
    """Deep-convert HfApi objects to the plain-JSON types the HTTP API returns.

    The HTTP spaces API hands back plain JSON, but the HfApi path yields
    SpaceInfo objects whose nested fields (RepoSibling, datetimes, card data)
    are not JSON-serializable. Round-tripping through json normalizes the
    HfApi path to the same shape, so AppInfo.extra is always plain data.
    """

    def default(o: object) -> object:
        if isinstance(o, (datetime, date)):
            return o.isoformat()
        return getattr(o, "__dict__", str(o))

    return json.loads(json.dumps(value, default=default))


def _coerce_space_data(value: object) -> SpaceData | None:
    """Return a string-keyed dict for space payloads."""
    if not isinstance(value, dict):
        return None
    return {str(key): item for key, item in value.items()}


def _coerce_space_list(value: object) -> list[SpaceData]:
    """Return only dict-shaped items from a raw HF payload."""
    if not isinstance(value, list):
        return []

    spaces: list[SpaceData] = []
    for item in value:
        space_data = _coerce_space_data(item)
        if space_data is not None:
            spaces.append(space_data)
    return spaces


def _get_string(item: SpaceData, key: str) -> str | None:
    """Read a string field from a space payload."""
    value = item.get(key)
    return value if isinstance(value, str) else None


def _get_card_data(item: SpaceData) -> SpaceData:
    """Read card data from a space payload."""
    card_data = item.get("cardData")
    return card_data if isinstance(card_data, dict) else {}


def _normalize_space_data(space_data: SpaceData) -> SpaceData:
    """Normalize HF API responses to the shape used by the app store."""
    normalized = dict(space_data)

    created_at = normalized.pop("created_at", None)
    if not normalized.get("createdAt") and created_at is not None:
        normalized["createdAt"] = created_at

    last_modified = normalized.pop("last_modified", None)
    if not normalized.get("lastModified") and last_modified is not None:
        normalized["lastModified"] = last_modified

    card_data = normalized.pop("card_data", None)
    if not normalized.get("cardData") and card_data is not None:
        normalized["cardData"] = card_data

    return normalized


def _build_app_info(item: SpaceData | None) -> AppInfo | None:
    """Build AppInfo from a normalized Hugging Face Space payload."""
    if item is None:

    item = _normalize_space_data(item)
    space_id = _get_string(item, "id")

def _load_app_metadata(app_name: str) -> dict:  # type: ignore
    """Load metadata for an app."""
    import json

    metadata_path = _get_app_metadata_path(app_name)
    if not metadata_path.exists():
        return {}
    try:
        with open(metadata_path, "r") as f:
            return json.load(f)  # type: ignore
    except Exception:
        return {}


def _find_metadata_for_entry_point(ep_name: str) -> dict:  # type: ignore
    """Find metadata for an entry point, even if saved with a different name.

    When apps are installed from HuggingFace, metadata is saved with the space name,
    but entry points may use a different Python package name (different separators
    or additional suffixes). This function searches for matching metadata.

    Returns:
        dict: The loaded metadata (may be empty if not found)

    """
    import json

    # First, try direct match by entry point name
    metadata = _load_app_metadata(ep_name)
    if metadata:
        return metadata

    # If not found, scan all metadata files to find a match
    parent_dir = _get_venv_parent_dir()
    metadata_dir = parent_dir / ".app_metadata"

    if not metadata_dir.exists():
        return {}

    # Normalize name for comparison (remove underscores/dashes, lowercase)
    def normalize(name: str) -> str:
        return name.lower().replace("_", "").replace("-", "")

    ep_normalized = normalize(ep_name)

    for metadata_file in metadata_dir.glob("*.json"):
        try:
            with open(metadata_file, "r") as f:
                file_metadata = json.load(f)

            # Get the space name from the file (filename without .json)
            space_name = metadata_file.stem

            # Check 1: Normalized name match
            if normalize(space_name) == ep_normalized:
                return file_metadata  # type: ignore

            # Check 2: Entry point name appears in siblings (package structure)
            siblings = file_metadata.get("siblings", [])
            for sibling in siblings:
                rfilename = sibling.get("rfilename", "")
                # Check if entry point package folder exists in siblings
                if rfilename.startswith(f"{ep_name}/"):
                    return file_metadata  # type: ignore

            # Check 3: extra.id contains normalized match
            extra_id = file_metadata.get("id", "")
            if extra_id:
                # Extract app name from full ID (remove author prefix)
                id_name = extra_id.split("/")[-1] if "/" in extra_id else extra_id
                if normalize(id_name) == ep_normalized:
                    return file_metadata  # type: ignore

        except Exception:
            continue

    # No match found
    return {}


def _delete_app_metadata(app_name: str) -> None:
    """Delete metadata for an app."""
    metadata_path = _get_app_metadata_path(app_name)
    if metadata_path.exists():
        metadata_path.unlink()

Пока идёт сборка (нужны сгенерированные типы) — разбор плана против фактического кода.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
**Ловушка идентичности оказалась точнее, чем в плане.** Демон при установке сохраняет весь `app.extra` в `.app_metadata/<space-slug>.json` и подмешивает его обратно в installed-листинг. Но на wireless-роботе используется ветка `_list_apps_from_separate_venvs`, где поиск метаданных — **строго по имени entry point** (`_load_app_metadata`), без фаззи-поиска из `_find_metadata_for_entry_point`. То есть у installed-приложения `extra["id"]` есть только когда имя entry point совпало со слагом Space; иначе в `extra` лежат лишь `custom_app_url` и `venv_path`. Нормализация самого демона: `lower().replace("_","").replace("-","")`.

**`current-app-status` действительно вернёт `null` — и generated-клиент на нём упадёт.** FastAPI отдаёт `AppStatus | None` → `anyOf: [AppStatus, null]`, а `Scripts/normalize-openapi.py:48` схлопывает null-ветку до голого `$ref`. Это ровно тот капкан, что описан в шапке нормализатора для `DaemonStatus.backend_status`, только для тела ответа — там нет `required`, который можно ослабить.

**Один и тот же `bg_job_register.ws_poll_info` обслуживает и `/update/ws/logs`, и `/api/apps/ws/apps-manager/{job_id}`.** Фреймы побайтово одинаковы, значит `AppsManagerStreamClient` — не «по образцу», а тот же клиент с другим URL.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

Что расходится с планом и требует решения:

| Находка | Источник | Следствие |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /install` → **400**, если `source_kind != hf_space` | `apps.py:73` | В спеке только 200/422 → придёт `.undocumented`, маппить явно |
| `POST /install-private-space {space_id}` → **401** без токена | `apps.py:220` | Штатный путь для приватных Spaces; в плане не был учтён — беру в M1 |
| `list-available` ходит в HF (таймаут aiohttp 30 с) | `hf_space.py:20` | Сессия generated-клиента — 3.5 с. Каталог по ней будет отваливаться |
| `PUT /startup-app` → 400, если приложение не установлено | `apps.py:201` | Отдельный исход в UI (M4) |
| `remove` сам сбрасывает startup-app | `apps.py:103` | Не дублировать клиентом |

Ветка тоже другая: план писался под `claude/hugging-face-oauth-app-store-5hu2g2` от `main@9404f7d`, фактический worktree — `claude/app-store-hf-remote-phase2-0463e5` от `e087bbd` (с влитыми known-robots). Работаю здесь, ничего не переношу.

Решения, которые принимаю сам (говорите, если против):
- Отдельный `Client` с 20-секундной сессией под `/api/apps/*` — иначе каталог не успевает приехать.
- `currentAppStatus()` не через generated-клиент, а сырым запросом с ручным декодом (прецеденты — `probeBackendReady`, `stlAsset`).
- Стрим job-логов — один общий тип с `UpdateLogStreamClient` (демон отдаёт буквально одни и те же фреймы), старое имя остаётся `typealias`-ом, UI не трогаем.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
`RobotAppStatus` и `RobotAppLockStatus` декодируются вручную, а не берутся из generated-клиента, по одной причине: в спеке `state` — закрытый enum, и значение, которое демон добавит в 1.10, уронит декодирование там, где его надо просто пронести дальше. Это ровно правило 3 проекта, и то же решение уже принято в `DaemonUpdateJob.Status` ([DaemonUpdate.swift:73](Sources/ReachyKit/Model/DaemonUpdate.swift:73)).

Побочный эффект, который стоит проговорить: `isBusy` для `.unknown` возвращает `true`. Неизвестное состояние — это состояние, о котором демон вообще сообщил, а он сообщает только пока приложение загружено. Ошибиться в сторону «слот занят» дешевле, чем предложить «Start» на занятом роботе.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

**Прошу вас написать один кусок кода** — это единственное место в M1, где есть настоящий выбор, а не следование образцу.

Файл [Sources/ReachyKit/Model/RobotApps.swift:159](Sources/ReachyKit/Model/RobotApps.swift:159), функция `matches(installed:)`. `self` — карточка из каталога, аргумент — запись из installed-списка.

Что известно точно:

| | каталог (`hf_space`) | installed |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | слаг Space (`reachy-mini-dance`) | имя pip entry point (`dance_party`) — автор выбирал независимо |
| `spaceID` | всегда есть (`pollen-robotics/reachy-mini-dance`) | **только** если демон нашёл свой файл метаданных |

На wireless-роботе метаданные ищутся по точному имени entry point ([local_common_venv.py:247](/Users/aleksei/Developer/reachy-mini-desktop-app-swift/.venv-sim/lib/python3.12/site-packages/reachy_mini/apps/sources/local_common_venv.py)), поэтому «имя не совпало → `spaceID == nil`» — обычный случай, а не экзотика. Сам демон в фаззи-ветке нормализует так: `name.lower().replace("_","").replace("-","")`.

Решения, которые за вами (5–10 строк):
1. Fallback на нормализованные имена, когда у installed нет `spaceID` — зеркалить демона или отказаться и считать «не найдено»?
2. Если `spaceID` есть у обоих, но они разные — это железное «нет», или всё равно пробовать имена?
3. Сравнивать нормализованный **слаг** (часть после `/`) или полный `owner/slug`?

Цена ошибки несимметрична: ложное «не совпало» покажет кнопку «Install» для уже установленного приложения (демон переустановит поверх — терпимо), ложное «совпало» отправит `stop`/`remove` **не тому** приложению.

Пока вы решаете — беру M1.2 (клиент), он от этого не зависит.

result.output:
# searchToolbarBehavior

## Overview
The `searchToolbarBehavior(_:)` modifier configures the behavior for search in the toolbar. It should be placed after the `searchable()` modifier that renders search in the toolbar.

## Purpose
This modifier changes the default behavior of a search field that appears in the toolbar. On iPhone specifically, the search field in the bottom toolbar can be configured to appear as a button-like control when inactive.

## Example Usage
```swift
@State private var searchText = ""

NavigationStack {
    RecipeList()
        .searchable($searchText)
        .searchToolbarBehavior(.minimized)
}
```

## Platform Availability
The modifier is available on iOS 26.0+ and later across all platforms:
- **iOS** 26.0+
- **iPadOS** 26.0+
- **Mac Catalyst** 26.0+
- **macOS** 26.0+
- **tvOS** 26.0+
- **visionOS** 26.0+
- **watchOS** 26.0+

## SearchToolbarBehavior Cases
The documentation content provided does not include the specific cases of `SearchToolbarBehavior`. However, based on the example shown, `.minimized` is one available case that collapses the search field into a button-like control when inactive on iPhone.

To view all available cases, you would need to reference the `SearchToolbarBehavior` documentation directly.

content.text:
Проверил по докам Apple, чтобы не гадать:

| API | Доступность | Что делает |
|---|---|---|
| `Tab(role: .search)` | **iOS 18.0+** | Роль search-таба; searchable-контейнер отдаёт поиск первому такому табу |
| `.searchToolbarBehavior(.minimized)` | **iOS 26.0+** | На iPhone поле поиска в нижнем тулбаре сворачивается в кнопку, пока не активно |
| `.tabBarMinimizeBehavior(.onScrollDown)` | **iOS 26.0+** | Таб-бар сжимается при скролле вниз |

То есть роль search-таба доступна уже на нашем полу (iOS 18, [Apps/Project.swift:30](Apps/Project.swift:30)) — availability-ветка нужна только для «кнопки вместо поля» на iOS 26. Вы правы по сути, но это не автоматика «при определённых условиях», а явный опт-ин модификатором после `.searchable`.

Текущий таб-бар ([ReachyRootView.swift:59](Sources/ReachyUI/ReachyRootView.swift:59)): **Robot / Live** (только iPhone и только при живом бэкенде) **/ Diagnostics**. План M4 клал магазин в `NavigationLink` внутри `RobotScreen` — то есть без своего таба. Вы предлагаете иначе, и это решение стоит зафиксировать до M4.

---
name: app-store-navigation-decision
description: The robot app store gets its own tab bar item, not a NavigationLink inside RobotScreen
metadata:
  type: project
---

Decided 2026-08-04, during Phase 2 (app store / Hugging Face / remote access): the
robot app store is a **fourth tab** in `ReachyRootView`'s tab bar (beside Robot,
Live, Diagnostics), not the `NavigationLink` inside `RobotScreen.controlSection`
that the written plan called for. Catalogue search is `.searchable` on the store
screen plus `.searchToolbarBehavior(.minimized)` under `#available(iOS 26)`.

**Why:** the store is a destination users return to, and the widget work (App
Intents, milestone M5) wants to deep-link straight into it. `Tab(role: .search)`
was rejected as overkill for a single screen — it earns its place only if search
ever spans catalogue + installed + "Your Reachies".

**How to apply:** a tab needs an empty state for "no robot connected", which today
only the Robot tab has (it falls back to `ConnectionScreen`). `TabRole.search` is
iOS 18+, so the role itself needs no availability branch; only
`.searchToolbarBehavior` and `.tabBarMinimizeBehavior` are iOS 26+.

M1 собран и проверен: **388 тестов зелёные, swiftlint 0 нарушений на 624 файлах, format-check чистый**. Идёт `build:app` (он же вернёт `Package.resolved` к 16 пинам).

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
Самое неожиданное открытие в `AppJobMonitor` — почему хватает **одного** курсора «сколько строк лога уже отдано», хотя источников два. Я ожидал, что WebSocket шлёт только новые строки с момента подключения, а поллинг — весь лог, и их придётся мёржить по содержимому. Но в `bg_job_register.ws_poll_info` сокет стартует с `last_log_len = 0` и на первом же пробуждении отправляет лог **с нулевого индекса** — то есть оба источника нумеруют одни и те же строки одинаково. Поэтому дедупликация сводится к «отдавай только то, чей индекс ≥ уже отданного», и порядок гонки между сокетом и поллингом перестаёт иметь значение.

Второй момент, ради которого стоило лезть в исходники: `.closed` на сокете **не является исходом**. Для обновления демона закрытие сокета — это и есть завершение (демон себя перезапускает), а для установки приложения демон остаётся жив, и закрытие сокета ничего не говорит об исходе — поэтому монитор продолжает поллить.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

@router.get("/central-robot-status")
async def get_central_robot_status() -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Proxy to the central signaling server's /api/robot-status endpoint.

    Uses the stored HF token server-side so the desktop frontend never
    sees the raw token. The frontend polls this to know whether any of
    the user's robots is currently held by a remote JS app, and if so
    which one (so it can show "In use by Hand Tracker" in the UI).

    Response shape:
        { "available": bool, "robots": [...], "reason": str? }

    `available` is false when:
      - no HF token stored (user not logged in)
      - central server is unreachable / returned an error
    Callers should treat `available: false` as "unknown, don't block".
    """
    token = hf_auth.get_hf_token()
    if not token:
        return {"available": False, "robots": [], "reason": "not_authenticated"}

    try:
        async with aiohttp.ClientSession(
            timeout=CENTRAL_ROBOT_STATUS_TIMEOUT
        ) as session:
            # Token goes in the Authorization header, not the URL —
            # otherwise it leaks into central's access logs and any
            # intermediate proxy's logs. The desktop frontend already
            # never sees the raw token (we read it server-side via
            # hf_auth.get_hf_token); header use keeps it off the
            # wire-visible URL as well.
            async with session.get(
                CENTRAL_ROBOT_STATUS_URL,
                headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"},
            ) as response:
                if response.status == 200:
                    data = await response.json()
                    return {
                        "available": True,
                        "robots": data.get("robots", []),
                    }
                if response.status == 401:
                    return {"available": False, "robots": [], "reason": "token_invalid"}
                logger.warning(
                    "[central-robot-status] unexpected status %s", response.status
                )
                return {
                    "available": False,
                    "robots": [],
                    "reason": f"http_{response.status}",
                }
    except (aiohttp.ClientError, asyncio.TimeoutError) as e:
        logger.debug("[central-robot-status] central unreachable: %s", e)
        return {"available": False, "robots": [], "reason": "unreachable"}

Все формы ответов подтверждены по исходникам демона. Два факта, которых не было в плане:

- `RelayState` в 1.9.0 — ровно 6 значений, **без** `unavailable`; седьмое (`"unavailable"`) добавляет сам роутер для Lite-робота и при отсутствии relay-модуля.
- `POST /refresh-relay` возвращает `{"status": "skipped", reason: relay_not_running|relay_unavailable}` — и докстрока демона прямо предупреждает: в этом случае клиенту **нельзя** ждать смены состояния relay, он не сменится никогда.
- `install_id` в `meta` — заявленное будущее поле, на 1.9.0 его нет; каскад ключей из плана обязателен.

Сначала переименую сессию под `/api/apps/*` — hf-auth ходит в интернет ровно так же (`whoami` на каждый `/status`), и ей нужен тот же бюджет.

questions.question: Как сопоставлять карточку каталога с установленным приложением?

options.label: id, иначе нормализованный слаг
options.description: Совпадение по spaceID, если он есть у обоих. Если у installed его нет — сравниваем lower().replace('_','').replace('-','') от имени entry point с так же нормализованным слагом Space. Разные spaceID — жёсткое «нет». Точно та же логика, что у демона в _find_metadata_for_entry_point.

options.label: Только по spaceID
options.description: Сопоставляем только когда оба несут id и они равны. Никаких догадок по именам: приложение без метаданных показывается как отдельная строка installed, а в каталоге рядом будет «Install». Никогда не попадёт в чужое приложение, но чаще врёт в UI.

options.label: Широкий матч по именам
options.description: Пробуем spaceID, а затем нормализованные имена всегда — даже когда у обоих есть id и они разные. Максимально мало ложных «Install», но есть реальный шанс отправить stop/remove не тому приложению.

git checkout Package.resolved 2>/dev/null; git add -A Sources Tests && git commit -q -F - <<'MSG'
feat: manage the robot's apps over the daemon's app-store routes

Wraps `/api/apps/*` and the lock route beside it, up to the point a screen
can be built on: a catalogue, an installed list, start/stop, and jobs that
report themselves honestly.

Four of the fifteen routes do not go through the generated client, each for
a reason the committed spec cannot express:

- `current-app-status` answers 200 with a literal `null` when the robot is
  idle. FastAPI types it `AppStatus | None`, and `normalize-openapi.py`
  strips the null branch the generator cannot handle — so the generated
  model is non-optional and throws on the one answer that matters most.
- `start-app`, `restart-current-app`, `robot-app-lock-status` and
  `job-status` return closed enums; a state a later daemon adds must be
  carried, not thrown (rule 3).

The catalogue also gets its own `URLSession`: listing it is an HTTP call
from the robot to the Hub, which the daemon budgets at 30 s, and the 3.5 s
health-poll budget the generated client runs on would never load it.

`UpdateLogStreamClient` becomes `JobLogStreamClient` with two addresses:
`/update/ws/logs` and `/api/apps/ws/apps-manager/{job_id}` are two routes
onto the same `bg_job_register.ws_poll_info`, frame for frame. That socket
only ever wakes on a new log line, so a job that finished before it opened
sends nothing ever again — `AppJobMonitor` therefore polls alongside it and
reconciles both against one "lines emitted" cursor, which works because
both sources report the log from its first line.

Identity between the two lists is the trap worth naming: a catalogue entry
is named after the Space slug, an installed one after the Python entry
point its author chose, and the daemon only carries the Space id across
when its metadata lookup — by exact entry point name on a wireless robot —
happens to hit. So the id decides when both sides have one, and only then
does the name get a say, normalised the daemon's own way. A missed match
offers "Install" for something installed; a wrong one would send `remove`
to somebody else's app.
MSG

feat: link a robot to a Hugging Face account and read its relay

Wraps `/api/hf-auth/*` — the robot's own token, the relay that token buys
it, and central's robot list proxied through it. The daemon's OAuth routes
are deliberately left alone: they exist for a browser pointed at the robot
and redirect back to `reachy-mini.local`, which is of no use to a client
that signs in natively and hands over a token it already holds.

Three shapes the spec does not describe, all read off `routers/hf_auth.py`:

- `relay-status` can answer `unavailable`, which is not one of `RelayState`'s
  six values — the router substitutes it for a Lite robot and for a build
  shipping no relay module. `isConnected` is taken as the daemon's own
  verdict rather than inferred from the state, so a value from a newer
  daemon cannot silently read as disconnected.
- `refresh-relay` answers `{"status": "skipped"}` when there was no relay to
  reconnect, and the daemon's own docstring warns that a caller which then
  waits for a state change waits forever. `RelayRefresh.didStart` is what
  makes that answerable.
- `central-robot-status` is a proxy, so the token never crosses the LAN.
  Every `available: false` means "unknown", never "no robots".

`CentralRobot` lands here rather than with the central client because the
proxy already serves it: its identity is `install_id ?? hardware_id ??
peerId`, and `peerId` changes on every relay reconnect. Daemon 1.9.0 sends
no `install_id` at all — the relay lists it as a future field — while
`hardware_id` is the same string `/api/daemon/hardware-id` serves, which is
what joins a central listing to a LAN one (rule 4).

git checkout Package.resolved 2>/dev/null; git add -A Sources Tests && git commit -q -F - <<'MSG'
feat: sign in to Hugging Face natively, with the token in the Keychain

This app gets its own Hugging Face session, separate from the copy a robot
keeps once it is linked. Signing in here is what makes "Your Reachies"
possible at all — central lists robots by whose token asks.

A public OAuth client with PKCE, pointed at the same endpoints and scopes
the daemon uses (`HF_OAUTH_SCOPES`), so one token covers the app store, a
private Space install and central alike. There is no client secret, because
a secret shipped inside an app is not one.

The daemon's own OAuth routes stay unwrapped: they redirect a browser back
to `reachy-mini.local`, which is no use to a client that signs in natively
and hands the robot a token it already holds.

Details that are easy to get wrong and are pinned by tests:

- PKCE is checked against RFC 7636's own vector. Padded or standard-alphabet
  base64 produces a challenge the Hub rejects as `invalid_grant`, with no
  hint as to which of the two mistakes it was.
- The callback's `state` is verified before the code is spent, and a
  mismatch leaves no token behind.
- The Hub answers with `accessToken` as often as `access_token` — the daemon
  reads both, so this does too.
- The form body is percent-encoded by hand: `URLComponents` lets `+` through
  in a query, and in a form body that decodes as a space, silently
  corrupting a verifier.
- A pasted token is validated against `whoami-v2` rather than pattern-
  matched, and travels in a header, never a URL.

The browser itself is not here — `ASWebAuthenticationSession` belongs to the
UI layer. `HFAccount` owns the parts that must be right either way, so the
model is exercised without opening anything.

Until the OAuth app is registered on the Hub the client id is empty,
`canSignInWithBrowser` is false, and the pasted-token path is the way in.
MSG

Две вещи в M3, которые стоят внимания:

**Форма запроса токена кодируется руками, а не через `URLComponents`.** `URLComponents.percentEncodedQuery` пропускает `+` как допустимый символ query — но в теле `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` `+` декодируется как пробел. PKCE-verifier из base64url содержит `-` и `_`, но refresh-токен Hub'а вполне может содержать `+`, и тогда обмен падает с `invalid_grant` без единой подсказки. input.prompt: Does Hugging Face OAuth support public clients / PKCE without a client secret? Is there any official SDK for native mobile apps? What redirect URI schemes are allowed — can a custom scheme like myapp:// be registered? Quote what it says about client secret and PKCE.

result.output:
# Sign in with Hugging Face

You can use the HF OAuth / OpenID connect flow to create a **"Sign in with HF"** flow in any website or App.

This will allow users to sign in to your website or app using their HF account, by clicking a button similar to this one:

![Sign in with Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/datasets/huggingface/badges/resolve/main/sign-in-with-huggingface-xl-dark.svg)

After clicking this button your users will be presented with a permissions modal to authorize your app:

![](https://huggingface.co/datasets/huggingface/documentation-images/resolve/main/hub/oauth-accept-application.png)

## Creating an oauth app

You can create your application in your [settings](https://huggingface.co/settings/applications/new):

![](https://huggingface.co/datasets/huggingface/documentation-images/resolve/main/hub/oauth-create-application.png)

### Public OAuth apps (no secret)

You can create or use OAuth apps without a client secret. This is useful for native apps, CLIs, or other contexts where keeping a secret is impractical.

- **At app creation**: When creating a new OAuth app, you can choose to create it without a secret.
- **After creation**: For an existing app, you can delete the client secret in the app settings. The app will then work as a public app.

Public apps authenticate using only the client ID (e.g. in device code or authorization code flows with PKCE). Apps that have a secret can still use the secret when needed (e.g. `Authorization: Basic` for token requests).

### If you are hosting in Spaces

> [!TIP]
> If you host your app on Spaces, then the flow will be even easier to implement (and built-in to Gradio directly); Check our [Spaces OAuth guide](https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/spaces-oauth).

### Automated oauth app creation

Hugging Face supports CIMD aka [Client ID Metadata Documents](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-ietf-oauth-client-id-metadata-document/), which allows you to create an oauth app for your website in an automated manner:

- Add an endpoint to your website `/.well-known/oauth-cimd` which returns the following JSON:

```json
{
  client_id:                  "[your website url]/.well-known/oauth-cimd",
  client_name:                "Your Website",
  redirect_uris:              ["[your website url]/oauth/callback/huggingface"],
  token_endpoint_auth_method: "none",
  logo_uri:                  "https://....", // optional
  client_uri:                 "[your website url]", // optional
}
```

- Use `"[your website url]/.well-known/oauth-cimd"` as client ID, and PCKE as auth mechanism

This is particularly useful for ephemeral environments or MCP clients. See an [implementation example](https://github.com/huggingface/chat-ui/pull/1978) in Hugging Chat.

## Device code OAuth

Device code flow lets users authorize an app on one device (e.g. a CLI) by entering a short code on another device (e.g. a phone or browser). No redirect URI or browser on the device running the app is required.

![](https://huggingface.co/datasets/huggingface/documentation-images/resolve/main/hub/oauth-device-first-step.png)

![](https://huggingface.co/datasets/huggingface/documentation-images/resolve/main/hub/oauth-device-second-step.png)

### Testing with a sample script

You can test a device-code OAuth app with the following script. Replace `<Client ID>` with your app’s client ID. For **public apps** (no secret), the script works as-is. For **apps with a secret**, add an `Authorization: Basic` header (Base64 of `client_id:client_secret`) to both the device and token requests.

```sh
#!/bin/bash
CLIENT_ID="<Client ID>"

# Step 1: Get device code
RESPONSE=$(curl -s -X POST https://huggingface.co/oauth/device \
  -d "client_id=$CLIENT_ID")

DEVICE_CODE=$(echo $RESPONSE | jq -r '.device_code')
USER_CODE=$(echo $RESPONSE | jq -r '.user_code')
VERIFICATION_URI=$(echo $RESPONSE | jq -r '.verification_uri')

echo "Device Code: $DEVICE_CODE"
echo "User Code: $USER_CODE"
echo ""
echo "Open: ${VERIFICATION_URI}"
echo "Enter the user code: $USER_CODE"
echo ""
read -p "Press Enter after authorizing..."

# Step 3: Get token
curl -X POST https://huggingface.co/oauth/token \
  -d "grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code" \
  -d "device_code=$DEVICE_CODE" \
  -d "client_id=$CLIENT_ID"
```

> [!NOTE]
> For OAuth apps that have a client secret, include an `Authorization: Basic` header (with Base64-encoded `client_id:client_secret`) on both the device code request and the token request.

## Currently supported scopes

The currently supported scopes are:

- `openid`: Get the ID token in addition to the access token.
- `profile`: Get the user's profile information (username, avatar, etc.)
- `email`: Get the user's email address.
- `read-billing`: Know whether the user has a payment method set up.
- `read-repos`: Get read access to the user's personal repos.
- `gated-repos`: Get read access to the content of public gated repos the user has been granted access to. Unlike `read-repos`, this does not grant access to private repos.
- `contribute-repos`: Can create repositories and access those created by this app. Cannot access any other repositories unless additional permissions are granted.
- `write-repos`: Get write/read access to the user's personal repos.
- `manage-repos`: Get full access to the user's personal repos. Also grants repo creation and deletion.
- `read-collections`: Get read access to the user's personal collections.
- `write-collections`: Get write/read access to the user's personal collections. Also grants collection creation and deletion.
- `inference-api`: Get access to the [Inference Providers](https://huggingface.co/docs/inference-providers/index), you will be able to make inference requests on behalf of the user.
- `jobs`: Run [jobs](https://huggingface.co/docs/huggingface_hub/main/en/guides/jobs)
- `webhooks`: Manage [webhooks](https://huggingface.co/docs/huggingface_hub/main/en/guides/webhooks)
- `write-discussions`: Open discussions and Pull Requests on behalf of the user as well as interact with discussions (including reactions, posting/editing comments, closing discussions, ...). To open Pull Requests on private repos, you need to request the `read-repos` scope as well.

All other information is available in the [OpenID metadata](https://huggingface.co/.well-known/openid-configuration).

> [!WARNING]
> Please contact us if you need any extra scopes.

## Accessing organization resources

By default, the oauth app does not need to access organization resources.

But some scopes like `read-repos` or `read-billing` apply to organizations as well.

The user can select which organizations to grant access to when authorizing the app. If you require access to a specific organization, you can add `orgIds=ORG_ID` as a query parameter to the OAuth authorization URL. You have to replace `ORG_ID` with the organization ID, which is available in the `organizations.sub` field of the userinfo response.

## Branding

You are free to use your own design for the button. Below are some SVG images helpfully provided.

Check out [our badges](https://huggingface.co/datasets/huggingface/badges#sign-in-with-hugging-face) with explanations for integrating them in markdown or HTML.

## Token Exchange for Organizations (RFC 8693)

> [!WARNING]
> This feature is part of the Enterprise plan.

Token Exchange allows organizations to programmatically issue access tokens for their members without requiring interactive user consent. This is particularly useful for building internal tools, automation pipelines, and enterprise integrations that need to access Hugging Face resources on behalf of organization members.

> [!TIP]
> If you only need keyless authentication from a CI/CD workflow (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, CircleCI, …) — without per-member token issuance — see [Trusted Publishers](./trusted-publishers), which also uses `/oauth/token` but takes an OIDC `id_token` minted by your CI provider as the subject token (no Enterprise plan required, no client credentials).

This feature implements [RFC 8693 - OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8693.html), a standard protocol for token exchange scenarios.

### Use cases

Token Exchange is designed for scenarios where your organization needs to:

- **Build internal platforms**: Create dashboards or portals that access Hugging Face resources on behalf of your team members, without requiring each user to manually authenticate.
- **Automate CI/CD pipelines**: Issue short-lived, scoped tokens for automated workflows that need to push models or datasets to organization repositories.
- **Integrate with enterprise identity systems**: Bridge your existing identity provider with Hugging Face by issuing tokens based on your internal user directory.
- **Implement custom access controls**: Build middleware that issues tokens with specific scopes based on your organization's internal policies.

### How it works

1. Your organization has an OAuth application bound to your organization with the `token-exchange` privilege.
2. Your backend service authenticates with this OAuth app using client credentials.
3. Your service requests an access token for a specific organization member (identified by email).
4. Hugging Face verifies the user is a member of your organization and issues a scoped token.
5. The issued token can only access resources within your organization's scope.

### Prerequisites

To use Token Exchange, you need an organization-bound OAuth application with the `token-exchange` privilege. Contact Hugging Face support to set up an eligible OAuth app for your organization.

Once configured, you will receive:
- A **Client ID** (e.g., `a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890`)
- A **Client Secret** (keep this secure!)

> [!WARNING]
> Organization administrators can manage the OAuth app after creation, including refreshing the client secret and configuring the token duration.

### Authentication

Token Exchange uses HTTP Basic Authentication with your OAuth app credentials. Create the authorization header by Base64-encoding your `client_id:client_secret`:

```bash
# Create the authorization header
export CLIENT_ID="your-client-id"
export CLIENT_SECRET="your-client-secret"
export AUTH_HEADER=$(echo -n "${CLIENT_ID}:${CLIENT_SECRET}" | base64)
```

### Issuing tokens by email

To issue an access token for an organization member using their email address:

```bash
curl -X POST "https://huggingface.co/oauth/token" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${AUTH_HEADER}" \
  -d "grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange" \
  -d "subject_token=user@yourorg.com" \
  -d "subject_token_type=urn:huggingface:token-type:user-email"
```

### Response

A successful request returns an access token:

```json
{
  "access_token": "hf_oauth_...",
  "token_type": "bearer",
  "expires_in": 28800,
  "scope": "openid profile email read-repos",
  "id_token": "eyJhbGciOiJS...",
  "issued_token_type": "urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:access_token"
}
```

The `id_token` field is included when the `openid` scope is requested.

You can then use this token to make API requests on behalf of the user:

```bash
curl "https://huggingface.co/api/whoami-v2" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

### Scope control

By default, issued tokens inherit all scopes configured on the OAuth app. You can request specific scopes by adding the `scope` parameter. See [Currently supported scopes](#currently-supported-scopes) for available values.

The token's effective permissions are limited both by the requested scope and by the user's role within the organization.

```bash
curl -X POST "https://huggingface.co/oauth/token" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${AUTH_HEADER}" \
  -d "grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange" \
  -d "subject_token=user@yourorg.com" \
  -d "subject_token_type=urn:huggingface:token-type:user-email" \
  -d "scope=openid profile"
```

> [!TIP]
> Follow the principle of least privilege: request only the scopes your application actually needs.

### Security considerations

Tokens issued via Token Exchange have built-in security restrictions:

- **Organization-scoped**: Tokens can only access resources within your organization (models, datasets, Spaces, and collections owned by the org). Outside the org, access is read-only and limited to: public collections from any user or organization, and public gated repos the user has been individually granted access to.
- **No personal access**: Tokens cannot access the user's personal private repositories or private repos from other organizations.
- **Short-lived**: Tokens expire after 8 hours by default. Organization administrators can configure the token duration (up to 30 days) in the OAuth app settings. No refresh tokens are provided.
- **Auditable**: All token exchanges are logged and visible in your organization's [audit logs](./audit-logs).

> [!WARNING]
> Protect your OAuth app credentials carefully. Anyone with access to your client secret can issue tokens for any member of your organization.

### Error responses

| Error | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `invalid_client` | Client is not authorized to use token exchange, or the app is not bound to an organization |
| `invalid_grant` | User not found in the bound organization |
| `invalid_scope` | Requested scope is not valid |

### Reference

**Grant type:**
```
urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange
```

**Request parameter (`subject_token_type`):**

| Value | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `urn:huggingface:token-type:user-email` | Identify the user by their email address |

**Response field (`issued_token_type`):**

| Value | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:access_token` | Indicates an access token was issued |

**Related documentation:**
- [RFC 8693 - OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8693.html)
- [Audit Logs](./audit-logs)
